item.title: TikTok Finalizing Trio of Settlements in Addiction Litigation
item.description: TikTok is finalizing agreements to settle three upcoming trials related to allegations that its video product is addictive and harmful to minors.

item.title: Citadel Securities’ Shah Says Markets Questioning Warsh’s Plans
item.description: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh is creating fresh uncertainty for investors by pledging to rein in inflation without explaining how he intends to do so, according to Citadel Securities.

item.title: Aging Farm Fleet Points to Recovery Starting Next Year, CNH Says
item.description: The farm machinery sector is primed for a rebound in 2027 as the current fleet ages and prompts growers to upgrade, according to tractor maker CNH Industrial NV.

item.title: Venezuela Oil Flows Drop as Iran War Pause Cools Indian Appetite
item.description: Oil exports from Venezuela plunged in July due to weaker demand from India after a pause in the Iran war unlocked Middle Eastern barrels trapped in the Persian Gulf.

item.title: Brazil’s Oil Output Hits Record as War Drives Up Non-OPEC Supply
item.description: Oil production in Brazil reached a record high in June as rising supplies from producers a world away from the Middle East cushion disruption from the fallout of the war in Iran.

item.title: Amazon Cloud Chief Says Potential AI Business is ‘Just Massive’
item.description: Amazon.com Inc.’s cloud chief said customers are starting to shift from using the company’s services to train AI models to integrating them into their businesses — fueling demand for a process known as inference.

item.title: India Seeks to Raise at Least $1.3 Billion in LIC Share Sale
item.description: The Indian government is looking to sell at least 2.5% stake in Life Insurance Corp. as part of its plan to meet the minimum public float rules.

item.title: The Forward Guidance Canard
item.description: What we need is a reaction function.

item.title: Central Banks Let Markets Do Heavy Lifting as Iran War Adds Risk
item.description: Some of the world’s biggest central banks seem happy to let bond markets do their policy work for them.

item.title: Colombian Peso Pares Stellar Rally as Central Bank Steps In
item.description: The Colombian peso is on track for its biggest drop in three months after the central bank unexpectedly paused rate hikes and announced a program to build up dollar reserves, signaling that the currency’s rally has gone too far.

item.title: FalconX Cuts Staff on Extended Downturn in Crypto Markets
item.description: Digital assets brokerage firm FalconX has cut 10% of staff globally, as it prepares for a prolonged downturn in cryptocurrency markets, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: India Raises Fuel Export Tax to Build Buffer as Wars Curb Supply
item.description: India increased levies on exports of oil products to bolster domestic fuel stockpiles while global supplies remained tight despite a pause in fighting between the US and Iran.

item.title: Citadel Securities Sees a $500 Billion Chip Financing Debt Binge
item.description: The credit markets may have had their fill of record borrowing for data centers, but tech companies aren’t done yet. Citadel Securities LLC is forecasting another $500 billion-plus of debt in the public and private markets by 2028 to bankroll the chips that go inside the artificial intelligence campuses.

item.title: Sequoia Leads $1 Billion Funding Round for Nuclear Startup Valar
item.description: Sequoia Capital led a $1 billion funding round for Valar Atomics Inc. that the nuclear startup says will help it shift from demonstrating small reactors to producing them in volume.

item.title: India Eyes More Tax Breaks for Electronics in Win For Apple
item.description: India is seeking to extend tax breaks to foreign firms that provide machinery to local electronics manufacturers in a move that will boost companies such as Apple Inc. and Google as they ramp up domestic production.

item.title: Robinhood Private Company Fund to Back Y Combinator Startups
item.description: Robinhood Markets Inc. kicked off formal marketing of its second publicly traded closed-end fund, which will focus on investing in private companies that have participated in startup accelerator Y Combinator’s programs.

item.title: Wildfires Fan Record Sales of Catastrophe Bonds to Backstop Risk
item.description: Insurers are turning to catastrophe bonds to pass on historic levels of wildfire risk to the capital markets.

item.title: US Copper Inflows Surge as Market Awaits Trump Tariff Call
item.description: Copper is pouring into the US at the fastest rate in at least 12 years as traders position ahead of President Donald Trump’s decision on tariffs on refined imports.

item.title: Senators Urge CFTC to Curb Wildfire Prediction Market Bets Over Arson Concerns
item.description: A group of Democratic senators urged the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to rein in prediction market trading on wildfires, expressing concern that individuals could be tempted to commit arson to make their bets pay off.

item.title: Australian Watchdog Proposes More Flexibility for IPO Marketing
item.description: Companies planning to go public in Australia may gain greater freedom to market themselves before filing a prospectus under new proposals from the nation’s financial regulator.

item.title: US Factory Activity Expands at Strongest Pace Since 2022
item.description: US manufacturing activity expanded in July at the fastest pace in more than four years as demand remained strong, production surged and firms added workers.

item.title: Amazon Joins Elite List of Stocks to Top $3 Trillion in Value
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. surpassed $3 trillion in market value for the first time, becoming only the fifth company to ever reach the milestone.

item.title: BofA’s Cabana Sees Risk in Silent Fed: ‘You Can’t Fool the Bond’
item.description: US Treasuries will resume their retreat if the Federal Reserve can’t do a better job communicating how it will meet its 2% inflation target, Bank of America’s Mark Cabana said.

item.title: Chile Economic Activity Caps Second Quarter on Stronger Note
item.description: Chile’s economic activity grew more than expected in June, providing President José Antonio Kast some respite at the end of an otherwise weak quarter as he moves to address headwinds such as high unemployment.

item.title: Brazil Analysts Cut 2026 Selic Forecast on Eve of Rate Decision
item.description: Brazilian economists cut their 2026 year-end benchmark interest rate forecast as Latin America’s largest economy shows mounting signs of cooling down.

item.title: US Futures Climb as Focus Shifts Back to Earnings, Oil Slides
item.description: US stock futures rose into the first trading day of the month as attention turned to this week’s heavy slate of earnings reports.

item.title: India’s New Stock Closing Auction Sparks Confusion on Debut
item.description: India’s new system to discover end-of-day market prices got off to a confusing start, with traders trying to make sense of a spike in the NSE Nifty 50 Index stemming from the shift.

item.title: Dollar Drops Further as Yen Rebound Extends Fed-Driven Slide
item.description: The dollar extended its slide on Monday as a joint US-Japan intervention to support the yen added to losses triggered by last week’s Federal Reserve meeting.

item.title: China Signals New Era for Mining M&A After Zijin Gold Rethink
item.description: The recalibration of an attempted takeover deal reflects a more risk-averse approach from Beijing.

item.title: Trump Family-Linked Bitcoin Miner Posts Second-Quarter Loss
item.description: American Bitcoin Corp., the Trump family-backed miner launched last year just before the cryptocurrency tumbled from record highs, posted a third consecutive quarterly loss after a decline in the value of its holdings.
